questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: Commingling, as prohibited by Georgia license law, means:

answers.text: depositing client funds into the broker's personal or operating account
representing both the buyer and seller in the same transaction
advertising a property without including the brokerage firm's name
sharing a client's confidential negotiating position with the opposing party

explanations.a: Commingling is the illegal practice of mixing funds held on behalf of clients with a licensee's or broker's personal or business funds; all client money must be held in a designated trust account.
explanations.b: Representing both parties describes dual agency, a separate disclosure and consent issue, not commingling.
explanations.c: Omitting the brokerage name from advertising is a substantive regulation violation, not commingling.
explanations.d: Disclosing confidential information violates the duty of confidentiality, a separate fiduciary issue.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A Georgia licensee accepts a gift card from a title company in exchange for referring clients to that company. This conduct is BEST described as:

answers.text: legal if disclosed to the client at the time of closing
a violation of license law prohibitions on undisclosed compensation
permissible under a referral fee exception in Georgia license law
legal provided the gift card value is under $25

explanations.a: Even disclosure at closing does not cure a prohibited kickback; RESPA and Georgia law generally bar referral fees from settlement service providers.
explanations.b: Accepting undisclosed compensation from a third party for referrals violates Georgia license law and RESPA's anti-kickback provisions.
explanations.c: No blanket referral fee exception permits a title company to pay a licensee for steering clients.
explanations.d: There is no de minimis dollar exception that makes kickback payments lawful.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A seller's agent in Georgia knowingly overstates a home's square footage to a buyer who relies on the figure and suffers financial harm. The agent faces:

answers.text: only a civil lawsuit, with no license consequences if the buyer signed an as-is addendum
no consequences because listing agents owe their duties to the seller, not the buyer
potential license discipline by GREC and civil liability to the buyer
reimbursement only through the Recovery Fund, with no separate license action

explanations.a: An as-is addendum addresses physical condition, not affirmative misrepresentation; knowing false statements remain actionable.
explanations.b: Listing agents owe honesty to all parties; intentional misrepresentation triggers both civil liability and GREC discipline.
explanations.c: Knowingly making a false statement of material fact is grounds for license revocation or suspension under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25 and also exposes the agent to a civil fraud claim.
explanations.d: The Recovery Fund is a separate consumer protection mechanism; disciplinary action and civil liability are independent consequences.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: Which of the following would NOT constitute a violation of Georgia real estate license law?

answers.text: practicing as a salesperson without a current Georgia license
depositing a buyer's earnest money in the broker's personal savings account
soliciting a listed property after the listing broker has requested the soliciting agent to cease contact
accepting a commission in the amount specified in a written, signed listing agreement

explanations.a: Practicing real estate without a valid license is a serious violation of O.C.G.A. § 43-40.
explanations.b: Depositing client funds into a personal account constitutes illegal commingling under Georgia license law.
explanations.c: Continuing to contact a seller after the listing broker objects is an unfair practice under GREC regulations.
explanations.d: Accepting the compensation agreed upon in a lawfully executed listing agreement is entirely proper and does not violate license law.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.keyword: salesperson must work under qualifying broker
questions.text: Under Georgia license law, a real estate salesperson must perform all licensed activities under the supervision of a:

answers.text: Georgia Real Estate Appraiser licensed under Title 43
qualifying broker licensed in Georgia
member of the National Association of REALTORS® in good standing
Georgia Bar-licensed real estate attorney

explanations.a: A real estate appraiser is separately licensed and has no authority to supervise a salesperson's brokerage activities.
explanations.b: Georgia law requires every salesperson to be affiliated with and work under a Georgia-licensed qualifying broker.
explanations.c: NAR membership is voluntary and confers no legal supervisory authority over licensees.
explanations.d: Attorneys licensed to practice law in Georgia may be exempt from real estate licensure in some circumstances but do not supervise salespersons.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: Georgia license law requires written agency disclosure in real estate transactions so that the parties are:

answers.text: automatically protected from legal liability for misrepresentations made prior to signing
entitled to choose their own closing attorney at the seller's expense
informed about which licensee represents whom in the transaction
guaranteed a minimum inspection period before any contract becomes binding

explanations.a: Agency disclosure does not immunize a licensee from liability for misrepresentation.
explanations.b: Selecting a closing attorney is negotiable between the parties; it is not a function of agency disclosure.
explanations.c: The purpose of mandatory agency disclosure is to ensure that buyers and sellers know whose interests each licensee is representing before substantive negotiation begins.
explanations.d: Inspection periods are negotiated contract terms; they are not a consequence of agency disclosure.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: Under Georgia GREC regulations, a qualifying broker must retain transaction records — including contracts and closing documents — for a minimum of:

answers.text: one year after the transaction closing
ten years after the transaction closing
six months after the transaction closing
three years after the transaction closing

explanations.a: One year is below the minimum retention requirement set by GREC regulations.
explanations.b: Ten years far exceeds the regulatory minimum, though keeping records longer is permissible.
explanations.c: Six months is insufficient; GREC requires a longer retention period to allow for investigation of complaints.
explanations.d: GREC regulations require qualifying brokers to maintain transaction records, including contracts and correspondence, for at least three years.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: Under Georgia license law, a qualifying broker who fails to properly supervise an affiliated salesperson may face:

answers.text: GREC disciplinary action even if the broker did not personally participate in the violation
mandatory retaking of the broker's licensing examination as a remedial measure
civil contempt proceedings only if the violation involved a client's funds
automatic conversion of the broker's active license to inactive status pending investigation

explanations.a: Georgia license law holds qualifying brokers responsible for supervising affiliated licensees; failure to do so can result in GREC discipline regardless of whether the broker was personally involved in the violation.
explanations.b: Retaking the licensing exam is not a standard penalty for supervisory failures.
explanations.c: Civil contempt is a judicial remedy for defying court orders, not the standard consequence for inadequate supervision.
explanations.d: Conversion to inactive status is not an automatic consequence; the Commission must act after notice and an opportunity to respond.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: To qualify for a Georgia real estate salesperson's license, an applicant must successfully complete a Commission-approved prelicense education course of:

answers.text: 25 hours
60 hours
75 hours
100 hours

explanations.a: 25 hours is the Community Association Manager prelicense requirement, not the salesperson requirement.
explanations.b: 60 hours is the broker's prelicense course requirement.
explanations.c: Georgia requires completion of a Commission-approved 75-hour Salesperson's Prelicense Course.
explanations.d: 100 hours is not the required course length for any Georgia real estate license category.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A Georgia salesperson who fails to complete the required 25-hour postlicense course within one year of the issuance of the license will:

answers.text: receive a written warning from GREC with a 90-day grace period to complete the course
be required to retake the salesperson licensing examination before continuing to practice
have the license placed on probationary status for six months
have the license lapse at the end of that one-year period

explanations.a: GREC does not provide a 90-day written warning grace period; the license lapses by operation of law.
explanations.b: Retaking the examination is required only when the lapsed licensee does not meet the reinstatement conditions; it is not the immediate consequence.
explanations.c: Probationary status is not the statutory consequence for failing to complete the postlicense course.
explanations.d: Under Georgia law, a salesperson who fails to complete the 25-hour postlicense course within the first year of licensure has the license lapse automatically.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: To qualify for a Georgia associate broker or broker license, an applicant must have been actively licensed as a salesperson or community association manager for a minimum of:

answers.text: three of the last five years
five consecutive years
two of the last three years
one year immediately preceding the application

explanations.a: Georgia requires applicants for a broker or associate broker license to have been licensed on active status for at least three of the last five years; time on inactive or lapsed status does not count.
explanations.b: Five consecutive years is more than the required minimum; inactive time would not count toward even five years.
explanations.c: Two of three years falls short of Georgia's three-of-five-year requirement.
explanations.d: One year is far below the minimum active experience requirement.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A salesperson passes the Georgia licensing examination. The license fee is $170 if applied for within 90 days of passing. If the salesperson applies between 91 days and 12 months after passing, the fee is:

explanations.a: $255 is 1.5 times the initial fee; the actual doubling penalty brings the fee to $340.
explanations.b: The license fee doubles to $340 for salesperson and community association manager candidates who apply after 90 days but within 12 months of passing the exam.
explanations.c: $170 is the fee only when applied for within the first 90 days.
explanations.d: $500 is not a fee amount specified in Georgia's licensing fee schedule.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: The Georgia Fair Housing Act protects which of the following as a class in housing transactions?

answers.text: profession or occupation
political affiliation
credit history or financial status
familial status, including households with children under 18

explanations.a: Occupation or profession is not a protected class under Georgia or federal fair housing law.
explanations.b: Political affiliation is not a federally or Georgia state-protected class in housing.
explanations.c: Credit history affects lending decisions but is not a protected housing class under fair housing statutes.
explanations.d: Familial status — including families with children under 18 — is a protected class under both the federal Fair Housing Amendments Act of 1988 and Georgia's corresponding law.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A Georgia landlord refuses to rent to a family because they have three children. This action most likely violates:

answers.text: both Georgia and federal fair housing law
only federal fair housing law, not Georgia's separate statute
only Georgia license law, not fair housing law
no law, because a landlord may establish reasonable occupancy standards

explanations.a: Refusing to rent solely because a family has children is discrimination based on familial status, which is prohibited by both the federal Fair Housing Act and Georgia's fair housing statute.
explanations.b: Georgia law tracks federal law on familial status; a violation of one is typically a violation of both.
explanations.c: Fair housing laws — not just license law — prohibit this conduct; a non-licensee landlord can also violate fair housing law.
explanations.d: Reasonable occupancy standards (e.g., maximum occupants per square foot) may be set, but an outright refusal based on having children is not a permissible occupancy standard.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: Under Georgia and federal fair housing law, an owner who personally lives in a dwelling with no more than four rental units and selects tenants personally may qualify for:

answers.text: an exemption from all state and local property tax obligations
the owner-occupant exemption that relieves certain small landlords from some fair housing provisions
an automatic waiver of GREC's agency disclosure requirements
a reduced examination fee when applying for a real estate license

explanations.a: Fair housing exemptions have nothing to do with property tax obligations.
explanations.b: The owner-occupant (or 'Mrs. Murphy') exemption permits owner-occupants of small rental properties (four units or fewer) to exercise personal discretion in tenant selection, subject to certain limitations.
explanations.c: GREC agency disclosure requirements are unrelated to fair housing exemptions.
explanations.d: Real estate license examination fees are not tied to rental property ownership status.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A real estate company instructs agents to describe the same neighborhood differently depending on the racial background of the buyer. This policy constitutes:

answers.text: a permissible internal marketing strategy if applied consistently across all agents
a violation of RESPA's anti-kickback provisions related to settlement services
illegal steering that violates both the Fair Housing Act and Georgia fair housing law
a violation only if a buyer can prove financial harm resulting from the differential description

explanations.a: Consistency in applying a discriminatory policy does not make it lawful; systematic steering is a per se fair housing violation.
explanations.b: RESPA addresses settlement service kickbacks; this conduct violates fair housing law, not RESPA.
explanations.c: Describing neighborhoods differently based on a buyer's race is textbook illegal steering under the Fair Housing Act and Georgia's fair housing statute, regardless of financial harm.
explanations.d: Proof of financial harm is not required to establish a fair housing violation; the discriminatory act itself is the violation.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.objective: 8E Real estate education, research, and recovery fund
questions.text: The Georgia Real Estate Education, Research and Recovery Fund is funded primarily by:

answers.text: fees collected from real estate license applicants
fines imposed on licensees who are disciplined by GREC
a percentage of the commission on every residential closing in Georgia
federal housing grants administered by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs

explanations.a: The Recovery Fund is capitalized by a portion of the fees paid by applicants when they obtain or renew real estate licenses in Georgia.
explanations.b: Discipline fines go to GREC's general operating budget, not specifically to the Recovery Fund.
explanations.c: There is no statewide commission surcharge that funds the Recovery Fund.
explanations.d: The Recovery Fund is a state-funded mechanism, not a federal grant program.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.objective: 8E Real estate education, research, and recovery fund
questions.text: Before a consumer may file a claim against the Georgia Recovery Fund for harm caused by a licensee, the consumer must first:

answers.text: file a grievance with the State Bar of Georgia and obtain an arbitration award
obtain a final, unsatisfied court judgment against the licensee
submit a written demand to GREC within 30 days of discovering the harm
exhaust all available proceeds under the licensee's errors and omissions insurance policy

explanations.a: The State Bar handles attorney disciplinary matters; a real estate Recovery Fund claim is a GREC matter requiring a court judgment.
explanations.b: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-22, a claimant must have a valid, final, unsatisfied court judgment against the licensee before seeking reimbursement from the Recovery Fund.
explanations.c: A demand letter to GREC is not the statutory prerequisite; an actual court judgment is required.
explanations.d: While other available remedies may affect the claim, obtaining a court judgment is the threshold requirement, not exhausting insurance first.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.objective: 8E Real estate education, research, and recovery fund
questions.text: When the Georgia Recovery Fund pays a claim on behalf of a licensee, that licensee's license is:

answers.text: placed on probationary status for one year pending repayment
suspended for 90 days while the Commission reviews the circumstances
automatically revoked upon payment of the claim
unaffected unless the licensee fails to repay the Fund within 60 days of notice

explanations.a: Probationary status is not the consequence; revocation is automatic upon fund payment.
explanations.b: A 90-day suspension understates the consequence; the license is revoked, not merely suspended.
explanations.c: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-22, payment from the Recovery Fund on behalf of a licensee triggers automatic revocation of that licensee's real estate license.
explanations.d: Revocation occurs at the time of payment, not conditionally upon the licensee's failure to repay within any grace period.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.objective: 8E Real estate education, research, and recovery fund
questions.text: A licensee whose license was revoked because the Recovery Fund paid a claim may petition for reinstatement only after:

answers.text: completing 100 additional hours of real estate continuing education
waiting the mandatory five-year disqualification period set by GREC
submitting a written petition to the Governor's office for executive clemency
repaying the full amount paid from the Fund, plus any accrued interest

explanations.a: Additional continuing education alone is not sufficient to reinstate a license revoked due to a Recovery Fund payment.
explanations.b: There is no fixed five-year disqualification; reinstatement depends on repayment of the Fund.
explanations.c: Executive clemency applies to criminal matters; reinstatement of a real estate license after a Recovery Fund revocation is handled by GREC, not the Governor.
explanations.d: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-22, a revoked licensee must repay the full amount disbursed from the Fund, including interest, before being eligible to apply for reinstatement of a real estate license.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A consumer who wants to file a formal complaint against a Georgia real estate licensee should contact:

answers.text: the National Association of REALTORS® Professional Standards Committee
the Georgia Real Estate Commission
the Georgia Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division
the Better Business Bureau's real estate dispute resolution center

explanations.a: The NAR ethics process is voluntary and handles ethical violations by REALTORS®; it is separate from Georgia's license law enforcement.
explanations.b: The Georgia Real Estate Commission is the state agency that receives and investigates complaints against licensees and has the authority to discipline them.
explanations.c: The Attorney General's office addresses consumer fraud broadly; license law complaints go to GREC.
explanations.d: The BBB is a private organization without legal authority to discipline or sanction real estate licensees.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: When the GREC investigates a complaint against a licensee, the licensee is generally entitled to:

answers.text: an immediate court injunction halting the investigation pending judicial review
a jury trial in the Superior Court of the county where the violation occurred
written notice of the complaint and an opportunity to respond before any final action
appointment of a state-funded public defender to represent the licensee at the hearing

explanations.a: Courts rarely issue injunctions halting administrative investigations; the licensee's due process rights are satisfied through the administrative process.
explanations.b: GREC proceedings are administrative, not jury trials; judicial review is available only after the administrative process is exhausted.
explanations.c: Due process requires that the licensee receive notice of the allegations and a meaningful opportunity to be heard before GREC takes final disciplinary action.
explanations.d: Public defenders are appointed in criminal proceedings; the state does not fund counsel for administrative license defense.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.keyword: GREC penalties available upon finding violation
questions.text: After a GREC hearing determines that a licensee has violated Georgia license law, the Commission may impose all of the following EXCEPT:

answers.text: revocation of the real estate license
a monetary fine for the violation
suspension of the license for a definite term
a sentence of imprisonment

explanations.a: Revocation is one of the most serious administrative penalties GREC may impose.
explanations.b: Monetary fines are among the civil penalties available to GREC upon a finding of a violation.
explanations.c: Suspension for a specified period is a standard intermediate disciplinary sanction.
explanations.d: GREC is an administrative agency and may only impose civil sanctions; imprisonment is a criminal penalty imposed by courts, not licensing boards.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A Georgia real estate licensee who receives a lawful GREC subpoena for records during a disciplinary investigation and refuses to comply may be subject to:

answers.text: contempt proceedings in a Georgia Superior Court
automatic license revocation without a formal hearing
a mandatory 30-day license suspension until compliance is achieved
federal criminal charges filed by the FBI for obstruction of justice

explanations.a: GREC subpoenas carry the force of law in Georgia, and a refusal to comply may be enforced through contempt proceedings in the Superior Court, which can impose sanctions to compel compliance.
explanations.b: Automatic revocation without a hearing would violate the licensee's due process rights; a court proceeding is required to enforce the subpoena.
explanations.c: A mandatory 30-day suspension is not the mechanism for enforcing subpoena compliance; court action is.
explanations.d: Defying a state administrative subpoena is a state law matter; the FBI does not prosecute non-compliance with GREC subpoenas.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.keyword: AMP assessment center locations in Georgia
questions.text: Georgia real estate licensing examinations are administered by computer at how many AMP Assessment Center locations in the state?

answers.text: 2 locations
8 locations
4 locations
6 locations

explanations.a: There are more than 2 AMP centers in Georgia; 2 is not the correct number.
explanations.b: Georgia has 4, not 8, AMP Assessment Centers.
explanations.c: AMP administers Georgia real estate exams at four locations: Lilburn (Atlanta NE), Marietta (Atlanta NW), Savannah, and Macon.
explanations.d: There are 4 centers, not 6.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A candidate who arrives more than 15 minutes after the scheduled Georgia real estate examination start time will:

answers.text: be allowed to test with a time extension equal to the delay
receive one free automatic reschedule to the next available date
be admitted if seats remain available in the testing room
not be admitted and will forfeit the examination fee

explanations.a: No time extension is granted; the candidate is simply not admitted.
explanations.b: Arriving late is treated as a missed appointment; there is no free automatic reschedule, and the fee is forfeited.
explanations.c: Seat availability is irrelevant; the 15-minute rule applies regardless of testing room capacity.
explanations.d: AMP policy is explicit: a candidate who arrives more than 15 minutes late will not be admitted and forfeits the full examination fee.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.keyword: inactive license status no sponsoring broker
questions.text: A Georgia salesperson's license is placed in 'inactive' status when the salesperson:

answers.text: is not affiliated with a sponsoring broker
fails to complete continuing education in the current renewal period
receives a formal reprimand from the GREC
voluntarily requests inactive status while under investigation

explanations.a: Under Georgia law, a salesperson's license is 'inactive' when it is not affiliated with and held by a sponsoring broker; an inactive licensee may not engage in real estate activities for compensation.
explanations.b: Failure to complete continuing education risks license lapse, not inactive status.
explanations.c: A formal reprimand is a disciplinary sanction that does not automatically change the license to inactive.
explanations.d: Requesting inactive status during an investigation is a separate procedural action; inactive status is most commonly the result of simply not having a sponsoring broker.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: Under Georgia license law, the primary responsibility of a qualifying broker with respect to affiliated licensees is to:

answers.text: personally review and countersign every purchase contract before the client receives a copy
supervise all licensed activities of affiliated licensees and ensure compliance with Georgia license law
guarantee that every affiliated licensee maintains an active errors and omissions insurance policy
provide each affiliated licensee with a dedicated office, phone, and business email account

explanations.a: Georgia does not require the broker to countersign every contract before client delivery; the duty is supervision of licensed activities generally.
explanations.b: Georgia law makes the qualifying broker responsible for supervising all licensed activities conducted by affiliated licensees and for ensuring that the firm operates in compliance with license law.
explanations.c: E&O insurance requirements, if any, are an individual licensee obligation; the broker is not the guarantor of each licensee's coverage.
explanations.d: Providing physical office infrastructure may be a business decision but is not the legally mandated responsibility that defines the qualifying broker's role.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.keyword: activity requiring Georgia real estate license
questions.text: Which of the following activities requires a Georgia real estate license?

answers.text: an individual selling her own principal residence without a broker's assistance
an attorney advising a client on real estate contract terms as part of practicing law
a government employee disposing of surplus public property in an official capacity
a person negotiating the lease of commercial real estate on behalf of another party for compensation

explanations.a: Owners selling their own property are expressly exempt from real estate licensing requirements.
explanations.b: Licensed attorneys acting within the scope of practicing law are generally exempt from real estate licensing requirements in Georgia.
explanations.c: Government employees acting in their official capacity to dispose of public property are exempt from the licensing requirement.
explanations.d: Negotiating the lease of real estate on behalf of another party for compensation is a licensed activity in Georgia; the person must hold a valid real estate license.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A person who acts as a real estate broker or salesperson in Georgia without a valid license may be:

answers.text: subject to criminal prosecution and barred from recovering any compensation through the courts
required to pay only a civil fine not exceeding $100 for a first offense
permitted to keep earned commissions if the principal ratifies the agreement in writing
exempt from prosecution if the transaction closed and the client was not harmed

explanations.a: Practicing real estate without a license in Georgia is a criminal offense under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-30, and courts will not allow an unlicensed person to recover compensation for real estate services.
explanations.b: Unlicensed practice is a criminal matter with potential misdemeanor or felony consequences, not a minor civil fine.
explanations.c: Principal ratification does not legalize unlicensed practice or restore the right to recover compensation.
explanations.d: A successful closing does not provide a defense to unlicensed practice; the violation occurred in the act of practicing without a license.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.keyword: attorney exemption from real estate licensure
questions.text: Under Georgia law, which of the following persons is most likely EXEMPT from the real estate licensing requirement?

answers.text: a property manager who negotiates leases for multiple clients and charges a monthly management fee
an attorney who negotiates a real estate contract for a client as part of the practice of law
a salaried employee who negotiates commercial leases on behalf of an outside investor
a person who shows properties and presents offers on behalf of a broker for compensation

explanations.a: A property manager who charges fees to manage multiple clients' properties is generally required to hold a real estate license in Georgia.
explanations.b: Georgia's license law exempts licensed attorneys performing real estate activities incidental to the lawful practice of law.
explanations.c: Negotiating commercial leases for an outside investor — even as a salaried employee — typically requires a license because the employee is representing another party's real estate interests.
explanations.d: Showing properties and presenting offers for compensation are core licensed activities; this person must hold a valid Georgia license.

questions.name: State Laws & Rules (Georgia)
questions.text: A person who manages a community association in Georgia for compensation must hold:

answers.text: a Georgia salesperson's license with an approved property management endorsement
a Georgia broker's license with at least three years of residential management experience
a valid community association manager's license issued under Georgia's real estate license law
any valid Georgia real estate license combined with a nationally recognized CAI designation

explanations.a: There is no property management endorsement attached to a salesperson's license; community association management requires its own separate license.
explanations.b: A broker's license alone does not authorize a person to manage community associations for compensation; the specific CAM license is required.
explanations.c: Georgia law requires anyone who manages a community association for compensation to hold a valid Community Association Manager's license issued under O.C.G.A. § 43-40.
explanations.d: A nationally recognized designation (such as a CAI credential) does not substitute for Georgia's state-issued community association manager's license.
